title: Effects of Blackbirds (Agelaius phoenicius) on Stink Bug (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae) Populations, Damage, and Yield in Florida Rice
authors: Borkhataria RR, Nuessly GS, Pearlstine E, Cherry RH
location: Everglades Research and Education Center, Belle Glade, Palm Beach County, Florida, USA
design: 4 fields (17m x 86m), each containing one bird exclosure (17m x 17m, 1.27cm polypropylene mesh netting over PVC pipes) and one unenclosed control plot (17m x 17m). Cultivar 'Wells'. Planted 1 Apr 2010, main crop harvested 120 DAP, ratoon harvested 210 DAP. ANOVA with treatment, replicate, and interaction. Means reported as untransformed ± SD.
notes: n=4 independent replicates (fields). Yield measured from 20 subsamples (1-m row each) per plot, so 80 subsamples per treatment — the reported SD is across subsamples, not across 4 plot-level means. Stink bug data from 2 sweep samples per plot (8 per treatment). The ANOVA appears to test treatment against subsample residual rather than the Rep*Treat interaction, which constitutes pseudoreplication. Blackbirds in this system are primarily grain pests, not biocontrol agents — the study found NO effect of bird exclusion on stink bug populations or yield. Bird damage to panicles was significantly higher in controls (birds present) but did not translate to yield differences. The netting mesh (1.27cm) excluded birds but allowed invertebrate predators (dragonflies, spiders) to access exclosures. Microclimate differences were minor (<1°C temperature, 29% lower wind, 12% lower solar inside exclosures).

observations.unit: g dry weight per 1-m row sample (adjusted to 12% moisture by multiplying by 1.12)
observations.treatment_description: bird exclosure — 17x17m plot enclosed in 1.27cm polypropylene bird netting over PVC pipe frame, excluding all birds; birds not able to access rice or stink bugs
observations.control_description: unenclosed 17x17m control plot — birds (primarily red-winged blackbirds Agelaius phoenicius) had full access to rice and stink bugs
observations.notes: SD of 43.7 (treatment) and 36.5 (control) are across 80 subsamples per treatment (20 per plot × 4 plots), not across 4 field-level replicates. Yield ANOVA: F(1)=1.2359, P=0.2681 — NOT significant. Direction: exclosure yield HIGHER than control. This is opposite to expected biocontrol direction but consistent with birds being grain pests in this system (excluding them removes grain consumption). I re-checked the arm assignment — confirmed correct: exclosure = treatment, open = control. The paper concludes blackbirds have little effect on yield.

moderators.pest_taxon: Oebalus spp. (rice stink bugs: O. pugnax 97% of adults, O. ypsilongriseus, O. insularis)

observations.notes: ANOVA: F(1)=0.1815, P=0.6814 — NOT significant. Expected direction: excluding predators should increase pest abundance. Here, pest abundance is slightly LOWER in exclosures, opposite to expected. Not significant — consistent with birds having no measurable effect on stink bug populations. 2 sweep samples per plot, so SD is across 8 samples per treatment, not 4 plot means. Stink bugs swept at heading (July 1).

observations.notes: ANOVA: F(1)=3.3469, P=0.1047 — NOT significant (borderline). Direction: pest abundance higher in exclosure, as expected if birds provide some biocontrol. But not significant. Swept October 25 at heading.

observations.tissue: grain (pecky rice from stink bug feeding)
observations.notes: Pecky rice ANOVA: F(1)=9.0186, P=0.0052 — significant. Pecky rice was LOWER in exclosures than controls — opposite to expected direction (excluding bird predators should increase pests and thus damage). However, the paper notes this difference was driven by a single replicate where pecky rice was nearly 2x higher in control than exclosure (39.6±7.8 vs 21.6±5.9%) despite similar stink bug numbers. Authors conclude the difference is not attributable to bird predation on stink bugs. I re-checked arm assignment: confirmed. SD is across 5 subsamples × 4 plots = 20 per treatment.

observations.tissue: grain (pecky rice from stink bug feeding)
observations.notes: Pecky rice ANOVA: F(1)=2.5782, P=0.1182 — NOT significant. Direction: slightly more pecky rice in exclosure, as expected if excluding birds increases stink bugs and thus damage, but not significant.
